read: full (the Khan Academy module lists and the 20 sample human-study problems were skimmed)
venue_now: NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks (p.1 footer); arXiv 2103.03874v2, 8 Nov 2021
what_it_is: MATH is 12,500 problems (7,500 train, 5,000 test) from high-school mathematics competitions such as AMC 10, AMC 12 and AIME, in seven subjects with difficulty levels 1 to 5; each has a full step-by-step solution in LaTeX and natural language and a boxed final answer (p.1, p.4). Models are scored by exact match of the boxed answer after normalisation rules (p.5), and by default are prompted to give the final answer directly (p.6). The paper also releases AMPS, a pretraining corpus of over 100,000 Khan Academy problems and about 5 million problems generated by 100 hand-designed Mathematica scripts (p.2, p.5-6). GPT-2 and GPT-3 models scored 3.0% to 6.9% (p.2, p.5).
size: 12,500 problems: 7,500 train, 5,000 test (p.4); GPT-2 (0.1B to 1.5B) and GPT-3 (13B, 175B) evaluated (p.5)
source_of_items: competitions (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME and others, collected via AoPS; p.4)
has_gold_traces: yes: every problem has a full step-by-step solution in LaTeX and natural language (p.1-2, p.4); the solutions are used for training and as hints (p.6, p.9), not to score model steps
evaluation: final answer: exact match of the boxed answer after normalisation (p.5); the default prompt asks for the final answer only (p.6)
human_validation: None reported for the items beyond curation by the competition community (p.13). A rough human baseline on 20 test problems by six university students, four of them authors, scored 40% to 90% (p.5, p.15).

engtrace_use.sentence: S-M1 (L155-161): In mathematics, benchmarks ranging from GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021) and Math (Hendrycks et al., 2021b) to HardMath (Fan et al., 2024), Putnam-Axiom (Gulati et al., 2024), and GSM-Symbolic (Mirzadeh et al., 2024) rigorously test abstract logical deduction and reasoning stability. S-I3b (L105-111): specialized benchmarks (e.g., Math (Hendrycks et al., 2021b) or HumanEval (Chen et al., 2021)) assess abstract logic and algorithmic translation.
engtrace_use.explanation: Right paper and right gist: MATH measures abstract, not physically grounded, mathematical problem solving. But 'abstract logical deduction' (S-M1) and 'abstract logic' (S-I3b) describe it loosely: the authors frame MATH as testing problem solving with heuristics, 'the ability to analyze a problem, pick out good heuristics from a large set of possibilities, and chain them together to produce an answer' (p.1; also p.4), and set it apart from logic tests such as LogiQA, on which large models already do well (p.13). 'Reasoning stability' does not apply to a static set scored once by exact match (p.5). The text also writes 'Math'; the dataset is MATH (p.1, p.4). For EngTrace the omitted point is that MATH already pairs every problem with a step-by-step reference solution but scores only the boxed answer (p.5-6), and its authors show a model giving the right answer with a wrong explanation (Fig. 3, p.7).

suggested_wording: MATH (Hendrycks et al., 2021b) collects 12,500 high-school competition problems, each with a step-by-step reference solution, and scores the boxed final answer by exact match.
facts_to_cite: 12,500 problems (7,500 train, 5,000 test) from competitions including AMC 10, AMC 12 and AIME (p.4)
Seven subjects and difficulty levels 1 to 5 following AoPS (p.1, p.4)
Every problem has a full step-by-step solution and a boxed final answer (p.1, p.4)
Scoring is exact match of the boxed answer after normalisation rules (p.5)
GPT-2 and GPT-3 models reached 3.0% to 6.9% accuracy (p.2, p.5)
Models can give the right answer with a misleading and wrong explanation (Fig. 3, p.7)
AMPS pairs over 100,000 Khan Academy problems with about 5 million problems generated by 100 hand-designed Mathematica scripts, 37 of which also generate step-by-step solutions (p.5-6)
A rough human baseline on 20 problems ranged from 40% to 90% (p.5, p.15)
overlap_with_engtrace: Shares: a step-by-step reference solution for every problem and an automatic, normalised final-answer check (p.4-5); difficulty levels 1 to 5 loosely parallel EngTrace's tiers (p.4). Its pretraining corpus AMPS generates about 5 million problems from hand-designed Mathematica scripts (p.5-6), a precedent for script-generated problems, though for training, not evaluation. Lacks: generated evaluation instances (static competition problems from public sources, p.4); step-level evaluation (boxed answer only, p.5); engineering or physical content; expert validation of the evaluator; contamination control.
notes: The May text writes 'Math' in S-M1 and S-I3b; the dataset name is MATH (Mathematics Aptitude Test of Heuristics, p.4). The finding that generating a step-by-step solution before answering lowered GPT-2 1.5B accuracy from 6.9% to 5.3% (p.5, p.9) is specific to 2021 models and should not be generalised. The reference entry (L1025) is correct; it could cite the NeurIPS 2021 Datasets and Benchmarks venue (p.1) instead of arXiv.
